source_refs.note: Exercise 10.4, Question 4 (5 parts): book pages 198-199 (PDF 203-204). No answer key (proofs). Verified with sympy and the solution book.

blocks.explanation:
Four cosines added; we must show the total is 0.
The trick is to pair them well. Angles that differ by \(180^{\circ}\) pair perfectly: their half-difference is \(90^{\circ}\) and \(\cos 90^{\circ} = 0\).
Plan: pair \(15^{\circ}\) with \(195^{\circ}\) and \(105^{\circ}\) with \(285^{\circ}\), using \(\cos P + \cos Q\).
steps:
Given: L.H.S. \(= \cos 15^{\circ} + \cos 105^{\circ} + \cos 195^{\circ} + \cos 285^{\circ}\).
To prove: L.H.S. \(= 0\).
Method: Regroup into two pairs and use
\[\cos P + \cos Q\]
\[= 2\cos\dfrac{P + Q}{2}\cos\dfrac{P - Q}{2}\]

Regroup
\[\text{L.H.S.} = (\cos 195^{\circ} + \cos 15^{\circ})\]
\[+ (\cos 285^{\circ} + \cos 105^{\circ})\]
Why: Addition can be done in any order. In each pair the angles differ by \(180^{\circ}\).

Add the pairs
\[\text{L.H.S.} = 0 + 0 = 0 = \text{R.H.S.}\]
Why: Both brackets are zero.

Check with allied angles
\[\cos 195^{\circ} = -\cos 15^{\circ}\]
\[\cos 285^{\circ} = \cos 75^{\circ} = \sin 15^{\circ}\]
\[\cos 105^{\circ} = -\sin 15^{\circ}\]
Why: The sum is then \(\cos 15^{\circ} - \sin 15^{\circ} - \cos 15^{\circ} + \sin 15^{\circ} = 0\) \(\checkmark\). (Pairing \(15^{\circ}\) with \(105^{\circ}\) also works, but needs \(\cos 240^{\circ} = -\tfrac{1}{2}\).)

blocks.explanation:
Four sines on top, four cosines below, with the same angles.
We must show the fraction is \(\tan 5\theta\).
Plan: pair the outer angles (\(8\theta, 2\theta\)) and the inner angles (\(6\theta, 4\theta\)); both pairs have half-sum \(5\theta\), so \(\sin 5\theta\) and \(\cos 5\theta\) come out as common factors.
steps:
Given: L.H.S. \(= \dfrac{\sin 2\theta + \sin 4\theta + \sin 6\theta + \sin 8\theta}{\cos 2\theta + \cos 4\theta + \cos 6\theta + \cos 8\theta}\).
To prove: L.H.S. \(= \tan 5\theta\).
Method: \(\sin P + \sin Q\) and \(\cos P + \cos Q\) on pairs chosen so that the half-sums are equal.

Numerator in pairs
\[\sin 8\theta + \sin 2\theta = 2\sin 5\theta\cos 3\theta\]
\[\sin 6\theta + \sin 4\theta = 2\sin 5\theta\cos\theta\]
Why: \(\frac{8\theta + 2\theta}{2} = \frac{6\theta + 4\theta}{2} = 5\theta\); the half-differences are \(3\theta\) and \(\theta\).

Take out the common factor
\[\text{Num.} = 2\sin 5\theta(\cos 3\theta + \cos\theta)\]
Why: \(2\sin 5\theta\) is in both terms.

Denominator in the same pairs
\[\cos 8\theta + \cos 2\theta = 2\cos 5\theta\cos 3\theta\]
\[\cos 6\theta + \cos 4\theta = 2\cos 5\theta\cos\theta\]
\[\text{Den.} = 2\cos 5\theta(\cos 3\theta + \cos\theta)\]
Why: Same angles, now with the \(\cos P + \cos Q\) formula.

Divide and cancel
\[\text{L.H.S.} = \dfrac{2\sin 5\theta(\cos 3\theta + \cos\theta)}{2\cos 5\theta(\cos 3\theta + \cos\theta)}\]
\[= \dfrac{\sin 5\theta}{\cos 5\theta}\]
\[= \tan 5\theta = \text{R.H.S.}\]
Why: The factor \(2(\cos 3\theta + \cos\theta)\) cancels (assumed non-zero).

Check: \(\theta = 10^{\circ}\)
\[\text{Num.} \approx 2.8356, \quad \text{Den.} \approx 2.3794\]
\[\dfrac{2.8356}{2.3794} \approx 1.1918\]
\[\tan 50^{\circ} \approx 1.1918 \;\checkmark\]
Why: Both sides agree.

blocks.explanation:
A difference of two squares of cosines.
We must show it equals \(\sin\alpha\).
Plan: factorise \(a^2 - b^2 = (a - b)(a + b)\), turn each bracket into a product with the sum-to-product formulas, then use \(2\sin u\cos u = \sin 2u\).
steps:
Given: L.H.S. \(= \cos^{2}A - \cos^{2}B\), where \(A = \frac{\pi}{4} - \frac{\alpha}{2}\), \(B = \frac{\pi}{4} + \frac{\alpha}{2}\).
To prove: L.H.S. \(= \sin\alpha\).
Method: \(\cos^{2}A - \cos^{2}B = (\cos A - \cos B)(\cos A + \cos B)\), then sum-to-product.

Half-sum and half-difference of \(A\) and \(B\)
\[\dfrac{A + B}{2} = \dfrac{\pi}{4}\]
\[\dfrac{A - B}{2} = -\dfrac{\alpha}{2}\]
Why: \(A + B = \frac{\pi}{2}\) (the \(\frac{\alpha}{2}\)'s cancel) and \(A - B = -\alpha\) (the \(\frac{\pi}{4}\)'s cancel).

The sum bracket
\[\cos A + \cos B\]
\[= 2\cos\dfrac{\pi}{4}\cos\left(-\dfrac{\alpha}{2}\right)\]
\[= 2\cos\dfrac{\pi}{4}\cos\dfrac{\alpha}{2}\]
Why: \(\cos(-u) = \cos u\) (cosine is even).

The difference bracket
\[\cos A - \cos B\]
\[= -2\sin\dfrac{\pi}{4}\sin\left(-\dfrac{\alpha}{2}\right)\]
\[= 2\sin\dfrac{\pi}{4}\sin\dfrac{\alpha}{2}\]
Why: \(\sin(-u) = -\sin u\), so the two minus signs cancel.

Multiply the brackets
\[\text{L.H.S.} = \left(2\sin\dfrac{\pi}{4}\cos\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)\times\]
\[\left(2\sin\dfrac{\alpha}{2}\cos\dfrac{\alpha}{2}\right)\]
Why: We rearranged the four factors (and the \(2 \times 2\)) into two double-angle groups.

Use the double-angle formula
\[= \sin\dfrac{\pi}{2}\cdot\sin\alpha\]
\[= 1\cdot\sin\alpha = \sin\alpha = \text{R.H.S.}\]
Why: \(2\sin u\cos u = \sin 2u\), and \(\sin\frac{\pi}{2} = 1\).

Check: \(\alpha = 60^{\circ}\)
\[\cos^{2}15^{\circ} - \cos^{2}75^{\circ} \approx 0.9330 - 0.0670\]
\[= 0.8660 = \sin 60^{\circ} \;\checkmark\]
Why: \(\frac{\pi}{4} \mp \frac{\alpha}{2} = 45^{\circ} \mp 30^{\circ}\).

blocks.explanation:
A product of two sines whose angles are \(\frac{\pi}{4} \pm \theta\).
We must show it equals \(\frac{1}{2}\cos 2\theta\).
Plan: make a factor 2 and use \(2\sin\alpha\sin\beta = \cos(\alpha - \beta) - \cos(\alpha + \beta)\); then \(\cos\frac{\pi}{2} = 0\).
steps:
Given: L.H.S. \(= \sin\left(\frac{\pi}{4} - \theta\right)\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{4} + \theta\right)\).
To prove: L.H.S. \(= \frac{1}{2}\cos 2\theta\).
Method: Product formula
\[2\sin\alpha\sin\beta\]
\[= \cos(\alpha - \beta) - \cos(\alpha + \beta)\]
with \(\alpha = \frac{\pi}{4} + \theta\), \(\beta = \frac{\pi}{4} - \theta\).

Create the factor 2 and order the factors
\[\text{L.H.S.} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[2\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} + \theta\right)\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} - \theta\right)\right]\]
Why: Multiplying by 2 and by \(\frac{1}{2}\) changes nothing; putting the bigger angle first keeps \(\alpha - \beta\) positive.

Find the new angles
\[\alpha - \beta = 2\theta\]
\[\alpha + \beta = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\]
Why: In \(\alpha - \beta\) the \(\frac{\pi}{4}\)'s cancel; in \(\alpha + \beta\) the \(\theta\)'s cancel.

Use the formula and simplify
\[\text{L.H.S.} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[\cos 2\theta - \cos\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{2}[\cos 2\theta - 0]\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{2}\cos 2\theta = \text{R.H.S.}\]
Why: \(\cos\frac{\pi}{2} = \cos 90^{\circ} = 0\).

Check: \(\theta = 15^{\circ}\)
\[\sin 30^{\circ}\sin 60^{\circ} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\]
\[\dfrac{1}{2}\cos 30^{\circ} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4} \;\checkmark\]
Why: Both sides agree.

blocks.explanation:
The same pattern as part (ii), with odd multiples of \(\theta\).
We must show the fraction is \(\tan 4\theta\).
Plan: pair \(7\theta\) with \(\theta\) and \(5\theta\) with \(3\theta\); both half-sums are \(4\theta\).
steps:
Given: L.H.S. \(= \dfrac{\sin\theta + \sin 3\theta + \sin 5\theta + \sin 7\theta}{\cos\theta + \cos 3\theta + \cos 5\theta + \cos 7\theta}\).
To prove: L.H.S. \(= \tan 4\theta\).
Method: \(\sin P + \sin Q\) and \(\cos P + \cos Q\) on the pairs \((7\theta, \theta)\) and \((5\theta, 3\theta)\).

Numerator in pairs
\[\sin 7\theta + \sin\theta = 2\sin 4\theta\cos 3\theta\]
\[\sin 5\theta + \sin 3\theta = 2\sin 4\theta\cos\theta\]
\[\text{Num.} = 2\sin 4\theta(\cos 3\theta + \cos\theta)\]
Why: Half-sums are both \(4\theta\); half-differences are \(3\theta\) and \(\theta\).

Denominator in the same pairs
\[\cos 7\theta + \cos\theta = 2\cos 4\theta\cos 3\theta\]
\[\cos 5\theta + \cos 3\theta = 2\cos 4\theta\cos\theta\]
\[\text{Den.} = 2\cos 4\theta(\cos 3\theta + \cos\theta)\]
Why: Same angles with the \(\cos P + \cos Q\) formula.

Divide and cancel
\[\text{L.H.S.} = \dfrac{2\sin 4\theta(\cos 3\theta + \cos\theta)}{2\cos 4\theta(\cos 3\theta + \cos\theta)}\]
\[= \tan 4\theta = \text{R.H.S.}\]
Why: The common factor cancels (assumed non-zero), and \(\frac{\sin}{\cos} = \tan\).

Check: \(\theta = 10^{\circ}\)
\[\text{Num.} \approx 2.3794, \quad \text{Den.} \approx 2.8356\]
\[\dfrac{2.3794}{2.8356} \approx 0.8391\]
\[\tan 40^{\circ} \approx 0.8391 \;\checkmark\]
Why: Both sides agree.
